text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL

- Resumption of efforts to achieve macro-economic stability and financial discipline in the economy should be main features of the future governing programme, central bank chief economist Daniel Daianu says.
- Sugar factories unable to pay back loans taken for upgrading projects.
- The Romanian Oil Company cannot supply the whole quantity of fuel needed by the farming sector.
LIBERTATEA
- Romanian banned livestock imports from Bulgaria following an outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease there.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Romania's first nuclear power plant at Cernavoda completed all tests and will be connected to the national grid by end-November.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Central bank expected to put in circulation new 50,000 lei banknote.
- Some 3,000 settlements in Romania are not connected to the national telephone system.
- Renel RA electricity authority owes its suppliers some 2.7 billion lei.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- High taxes on profit discourage foreign investors in Romania.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The presiding judge of a Bucharest polling station was cought reducing the number of votes for the opposition Democratic Convention (CDR) presidential candidate Emil Constantinescu.
- The newspaper alleges that a huge fraud is prepared for the November 17 runoff in the presidential poll.
- The Human Rights Defence League (LADO) said in many polling stations the number of ballots found in the boxes was higher than the number of voters who had voted.
- Fifty years after the installment of communism by fraud in the November 1946 elections, Romania in November 1996 becomes a centre-right state, says the newspaper on Sunday's general election.
ADEVARUL

- President Ion Iliescu will be the candidate of a defeated party, the Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) in the presidential run-off on November 17, what has a negative impact over his image, says an editorial on the November 3 general poll.
- The opposition CDR and Social Democratic Union (USD), winners of the parliamentary polls, could sign the governing protocol today.
- Petre Roman, Romania's first post-communist prime minister and USD leader, to get the Foreign Ministry, said sources close to the CDR and USD.
- More than one third of Romania's 4,000 people with AIDS have died, said Valentin Simion from the health ministry.
- Miron Cosma, the miners' union leader who led thousands of his colleagues to riot in Bucharest in June 1990 and September 1991, was elected as an independent senator in his county of Hunedoara.
- The newspaper publishes partial results from the November 3 poll in 28 of Romania's 42 counties.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- The newspaper presents a two-page report with frauds registered during and after the November 3 polls. It says the media struggles to disclose the huge fraud allegedly conducted by the ruling PDSR under the slogan "Steal for Ion Iliescu."
- Sorin Lepsa, vice-president of the opposition National Peasant Party (PNT-CD) said the CDR wants to change the system and is not interested in a "witch hunt".

- "From 'Down Iliescu' to 'Iliescu we love you' -- a typical career for a member of the ruling PDSR camarilla" reads the headline on a one-page report on former union leader Miron Mitrea turned PDSR vice-president.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Leaders of all parliamentary parties comment on the November 3 polls.
- Opposition USD will ask the votes and the annuled ones to be counted again and checked in the polling stations where irregularites had been reported.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The now ruling PDSR will stay in the opposition and has no intention to force early elections, said PDSR executive president Adrian Nastase.
DIMINEATA

- "Voting Ion Iliescu you vote for your family's peace and the country's stability" reads a front-page headline urging people to vote for President Iliescu in the November 17 runoff. ($=3,420 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
